title: WPMS/1840/2013 of B.S.NEGI MAHILA TAKNIKI PRASHIKSHAN KENDRA Vs DEPUTY LABOUR COMMISSIONER

paras.text:
WPMS No. 1840 of 2013
Hon'ble Manoj K. Tiwari, J.
Mr. Siddhartha Sah, Advocate for the
petitioner.
Mr. Vijay Khanduri, Brief Holder for
the State of Uttarakhand.
Mr. M.C. Pant, Advocate for respondent
no. 2.
Heard learned counsel for the parties
through video conferencing.
This writ petition has been filed by B.S.
Negi Mahila Takniki Prashikshan Kendra,
Dehradun. According to the petitioner,
name of the petitioner's Institute earlier was
"ONGC Mahila Polytechnic". Wilson Robert
(respondent no. 2) was an employee of the
said Institute, whose services were
terminated w.e.f. 28.03.1997.
Against his termination, respondent
No. 2 raised an industrial dispute, which
was referred for adjudication to Labour
Court, Dehradun and was registered as
Adjudication Case No. 155 of 1997. Learned
Labour Court on 16.05.1998 decided the
reference in favour of workman (respondent
no. 2 herein) and declared termination of his
service w.e.f. 28.03.1997 to be unjust and
illegal and directed the employer (petitioner
herein) to reinstate him with 50% back
wages.
It is the case of the petitioner that
award given by Labour Court was
challenged by filing Writ Petition No. 9955 of
1999 by the petitioner before Allahabad
High Court, which, after transfer to this
Court, was renumbered as WPMS No. 1393
of 2001. The said writ petition was decided
vide judgment dated 23.07.2008.
Perusal of the judgment dated
23.07.2008 reveals that the award was

modified and it was provided that although
direction for reinstatement will remain,
however, the direction for payment of 50%
back wages was set aside. Paragraphs 4 & 5
of the said judgment are reproduced below:-
"4. I do not find any illegality or
perversity in the impugned award passed by
the Labour Court and the same does not require
any interference by this Court. However, since
the factum of gainful employment of the
workman is undisputedly proved, therefore, it
would not be proper to award any back wages
to the workman respondent no. 2. the impugned
award dated 16.5.1998 is modified to the extent
indicate above.
5. In the result, writ petition is partly
allowed. the workman/respondent no. 2 shall
not be paid any back wages and the amount, if
any, deposited by the petitioner towards it shall
be released in favour of the petitioner. In the
facts and circumstances of the case, there shall
be no order as to costs."
Petitioner is aggrieved by the order
dated 12.0.7.2013 passed by Deputy Labour
Commissioner, Garhwal Division, Dehradun.
The said order is addressed to Collector,
Dehradun, whereby request has been made
to recover a sum of `5,84,859/- + recovery
charges from the petitioner. In the opening
paragraph of the said order, reference has
been made to the award dated 16.05.1998
rendered in Adjudication Case No. 155 of
1997.
It is contended on behalf the petitioner
that since the award passed by Labour
Court was modified by this Court in WPMS
No. 1393 of 2001, therefore, Deputy Labour
Commissioner could not have passed the
order for recovery of `5,84,859/- towards
back wages. It is further contended that in
terms of judgment of this Court, no amount

is payable to respondent no. 2, as back
wages, therefore, the direction to recover
such huge amount, as back wages from the
petitioner, is uncalled for.
This Court finds some substance in the
contention made on behalf of the petitioner.
In terms of judgment of this Court rendered
in WPMS No. 1393 of 2001, Wilson Robert
(respondent no. 2) is not entitled for any
back wages, therefore, petitioner is not liable
to pay any amount to respondent No. 2 as
wages between the date of his termination,
till the date of passing of award by the
Labour Court.
However, since there is no clarity as to
whether the amount sought to be recovered
is towards back wages or otherwise,
therefore, the matter is remitted back to the
Deputy Labour Commissioner, who shall
examine this aspect of the matter and take
appropriate decision, in accordance with
law, after notice to respondent no. 2, within
a period of six months from the date of
production of certified copy of this order.
With the aforesaid direction, the writ
petition is disposed of.
 (Manoj K. Tiwari, J.)
Aswal 05.12.2020
